script: Listen to the following conversation about a part-time job.
I'm looking for a part-time job on campus.
Then you've come to the right place. The campus employment office is here to help students like you find jobs on campus.
I'm glad to hear that, because I really need to start earning some money.
Let me ask you some questions. First of all, how many hours a week do you want to work?
I need to work at least ten hours a week, and I don't think I can handle more than twenty hours with all the courses I'm taking.
And when are you free to work?
All of my classes are in the morning, so I can work every weekday from noon on. And of course I wouldn't mind working on the weekends.

I'll try to match you up with one of our student jobs. Please fill out this form with some additional information about your skills, and leave it with me today. Then you can call me back tomorrow, and maybe I'll have some news for you.

script: Listen to a conversation between two friends.
Hi, Jack. It's good to see you again. Are you ready to get down to business after spring break?
Not really, but I don't have much choice, do I? It's going to be hard to get back to work, since I just had the most fantastic vacation ever.
I went kayaking on a river.
At first I was. But after I learned some techniques for maneuvering the kayak, it wasn't so bad. We didn't start out on the river. We had three whole days of instruction in a shallow pool first.
Did you spend the nights camping outside on the ground? That alone would make the trip unappealing to me.
Oh, no. The accommodations were fantastic. Each person had a private cabin, and there was a hot tub, a lodge where you could relax, and a top-notch cafeteria.
Now that part sounds good to me. But I don't think I'd like riding through rough water in a small kayak.
Oh, you should try it. I'm going to do it again as soon as I can afford the time and the money.

script: Listen to a conversation between two classmates.
Did you read the article that the professor assigned for tomorrow's class? It was really interesting.
No, not yet. What was it about?
It was about pollution, specifically one kind called acid rain.
Why is it called acid rain?
Because the rain, or some other kind of precipitation, has been polluted with acid.
Where does the acid come from?

From cars and factories, anything that burns coal or oil. These release sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. Sulfur dioxide reacts with water vapor to form sulfuric acid, and nitrogen oxides react with water vapor to form nitric acid.
So when coal or oil is burned, acid forms, and when it rains or snows, the acid falls back on the earth?

Exactly. That's why it's so dangerous. Acid rain has been falling over parts of northern America and northern Europe, and if this isn't checked, the effect on the water supply and on plant and animal life could be disastrous.
This is important. I really need to read that article.
